title: RE David C. Lachman et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specification #1 sustained (8,0,2); Specification #2 sustained (10,0); Specification #3 sustained (10,0). The adopted judgment annulled Philadelphia Presbytery's action in not sustaining its judicial commission's judgment and instructed Presbytery to advise the Calvary Session that physical cruelty is not biblical or confessional grounds for divorce.
first_summary: The General Assembly sustained RE David C. Lachman's complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery's failure to sustain its judicial commission's judgment concerning the Calvary Session. The commission had sustained three specifications that the Session's approval of divorce for physical cruelty violated Scripture, the Westminster Confession, and the church's disciplinary role. The Assembly annulled Presbytery's action and instructed it to advise the Session that physical cruelty is not biblical or confessional grounds for divorce. An explanatory opinion urged pastoral alternatives before divorce.
summary: Complainant elders challenged Philadelphia Presbytery's tie-vote refusal to sustain its judicial commission's judgment that the Calvary Session wrongly treated physical cruelty as biblical grounds for divorce. The General Assembly adopted the commission's judgment sustaining all three specifications: the Session's action contravened Matthew 5 and 19, WCF 24:6, and the church's disciplinary role. It annulled Presbytery's refusal and instructed Presbytery to advise the Session that physical cruelty is not biblical or confessional grounds for divorce. The explanatory opinion urged pastoral alternatives, such as separation and rehabilitation, before any divorce determination.

sources.supports: Full supplied case text: complaint excerpt, adopted adjudication, explanatory opinion, and Judicial Commission #3 minutes.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Source lines 1–5, 11–13, 19. The case is Case #3, RE David C. Lachman et al. v. Philadelphia Presbytery; the report of Judicial Commission #3 was heard, its judgment approved, and the report as a whole adopted by the 16th General Assembly.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 21–37, 47–81. Lachman complained against the Calvary Session's February 24, 1987 action treating physical cruelty as grounds for divorce and supporting the wife's divorce and deaconess status. After the Session forwarded the complaint, a Philadelphia Presbytery judicial commission sustained Lachman on November 17, 1987, but Presbytery failed to adopt the commission's judgment by a tie vote on January 9, 1988; Lachman then complained to the General Assembly.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 83–93, 169–177. The adopted adjudication sustained Specifications #1–#3, citing Matthew 5:31–32 and 19:3–9, WCF 24:6 with 1 Corinthians 7:10–11, and the denial of ongoing church discipline. The amends annulled Presbytery's failure to sustain its commission's judgment and instructed Presbytery to advise the Session that physical cruelty is not biblical or confessional grounds for divorce.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 11–13, 97–111, 133–185. The explanatory opinion is adopted pastoral commentary, not a separate holding; it suggests separation, possible restraining orders, rehabilitation, and later consideration of desertion but does not mandate those steps. The minutes at line 175 say 'June 8, 1987' though the Assembly and preceding minutes place the commission in June 1988; this apparent year typo is not relied on.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Lines 65–71. The November 17, 1987 judicial commission decisions sustaining Lachman's three appeals are incorporated as the lower court judgment; lines 85–87 and 171–173 restate those same three specifications as sustained.
